prompt_en: Vertical eye-level documentary medium-close photograph inside a warm maid cafe. One explicitly adult original human nekomimi maid in a covered navy frilled apron stands behind a wooden counter. Her baseline is brisk, guarded service. An adult customer's lightly bandaged hand reaches from the foreground for a steaming standard takeaway cup. Freeze mid-sleeving before the protective handoff is complete: her right hand holds the cup just beyond the customer's fingertips while her left hand slides a normal six-centimeter-tall corrugated kraft coffee sleeve only halfway up it. The sleeve fits snugly around the cup, its top edge remains visibly open, and it never becomes a bag or box. Her mouth forms a tiny huff and her face turns away, yet the compact ear nearest the customer pivots sideways toward the reaching hand while the far ear stays upright and forward; her eyes steal one reluctant glance back. The half-seated sleeve already protects the cup while the transfer remains unfinished. Her adult human face, forearms, five-fingered hands, short nails, frilled apron, and service role remain clear. Only two small living cat ears emerge organically through the hairline; no tail. Three-quarter frontal framing keeps both unequal ear angles, her face, both working hands, the customer hand, cup, and half-seated sleeve in one tight focal plane. Warm practical light, natural skin and fabric texture, cup steam, realistic contact shadows, shallow falloff. Nonsexual everyday comedy, observed rather than posed.
